title: In a growth case, find where growth can come from, then size and rank every option
description: The first question to ask in a growth strategy case, how to structure it, and the trap to avoid.
hook: Growth cases are open questions, which makes them easy to ramble through. A little structure turns them into one of the friendlier case types.
body:
The first question to ask

Growth from where: revenue split by business unit?

How to build your structure

  • Organic: more from current customers, new segments or regions, new channels, new products
  • Inorganic: acquisitions, partnerships
  • Choose: size each option, rank by value and risk

The trap most people fall into

A list of ideas with no sizing or priority.

For the full tree, with every branch, read the growth strategy framework.

Two prompts to try

How should a newspaper grow digital subscriptions?

Show a model structure
  • Reach: Traffic: search, social, newsletters; New audiences and topics
  • Conversion: Paywall design, trials, price; Sign-up friction
  • Retention: Engagement habits, apps, bundles; Cancellation process and win-back
  • Revenue per subscriber: Tiers, family plans, add-ons; Annual vs monthly

Where to start: The funnel: find the step with the biggest drop-off.

The trap: Only listing marketing ideas without the reach → convert → retain funnel.

How can a university attract more international students?

Show a model structure
  • Markets: Which countries have demand; Competition from other countries
  • Offer: Courses, price, scholarships; Rankings and graduate jobs
  • Recruitment: Agents, partners, digital; Conversion from offer to arrival
  • Barriers: Visas and policy; Housing and support

Where to start: Conversion from offer to arrival: many offers are lost to visas and competitors.

The trap: Ignoring visas and housing, which often limit numbers.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. Practise this case type in the free casebook: every case has a worked answer.
